sections.h2: Polyethylene starts to break down 142°C lower over a ZSM-5 zeolite

chart.title: A ZSM-5 zeolite lowered polyethylene's breakdown temperature by 142°C in a 2025 study
chart.sub: Temperature at which polyethylene starts to lose weight, °C.
chart.source: Energy & Fuels (2025), as cited in the post.

sections.means: Acid sites in the zeolite let polyethylene start to crack at a lower temperature, without changing the energy the reaction needs.
sections.todo: Refinery and pyrolysis operators should trial zeolite-loaded beds to hold their reactors at a lower, controlled temperature.

sections.h2: Oil is the largest output of India's tyre pyrolysis, at 41% by weight

chart.title: Of 2.68 Mt of tyres pyrolysed, oil is 41%, char 30% and steel 11%
chart.sub: Share of tyre pyrolysis output by weight, %.
chart.source: NITI Aayog (2026); this blog's division of the tonnages.

sections.means: Gas and losses take about 18% of the feed, which the reactor can burn to supply its own heat.
sections.todo: Sell the cleaned oil to refiners for hydrotreating, the route NITI Aayog points to for tyre oil.

sections.h2: In-reactor additives cut tyre-oil sulphur from 1.16% to as low as 0.38%

chart.title: Formulated red mud gave the lowest oil sulphur, 0.38%, against 1.16% in a 2025 study
chart.sub: Sulphur in the pyrolysis oil, % by weight.
chart.source: Studies cited in the post's tyre-sulphur section.

sections.means: Basic oxides such as lime and red mud hold sulphur in the solid char, so the oil leaves the reactor cleaner.
sections.todo: Test red mud and lime beds at a plant, then hydrotreat the oil, because in-reactor capture alone does not reach diesel quality.
